tools.name: rent_check
tools.description: Compares a weekly rent, and any proposed new rent, with how the ABS rents index for the tenant's Australian capital city has moved since the lease began. city is one of the eight capital cities, whose index is city-wide, not suburb-level. The answer is information, not advice, and carries the months compared, the source and the index's limits.

city.description: Capital city whose ABS rents index the rent is compared with

current_rent.description: Current weekly rent in Australian dollars

proposed_rent.description: Proposed new weekly rent in Australian dollars

tools.name: market_indicators
tools.description: Latest observed Australian property market indicators - RBA cash rate, unemployment, wage growth, rents by capital city, new housing lending, lending standards and arrears, dwelling approvals and completions - each with its period, source, licence and limits. Observed figures only; none is a forecast. geography, if given, narrows the answer to the figures for one place (e.g. NSW, Australia, Sydney).

geography.description: NSW, Australia, or a capital city

tools.name: data_sources
tools.description: The sources behind DwellDelta's figures, their licences, and what it cannot answer (what any one home sold for, the rent of a single street or home, rents by area outside NSW, Victoria, Queensland and WA, sale prices outside NSW, advice).

tools.name: vic_rents
tools.description: Victorian rents from Homes Victoria's Rental Report (CC BY 4.0): the median weekly rent of new leases in the latest quarter, how many leases it rests on, and the change on a year before, for 146 suburb groups and 13 regions. suburb_group (part of a name works, e.g. "Brighton") or region narrows the answer to the place the question is about. The figures are new-lease medians, not advertised rents, and each answer states its quarter, its source line and the source's limits.

suburb_group.description: A Homes Victoria suburb group, or part of a suburb name

region.description: A region, e.g. Inner Melbourne, Geelong, Ballarat

tools.name: area_rents
tools.description: Median weekly rent of new bonds lodged in the latest quarter, all dwellings together, with the bond count and the change on a year before, for one state per call: NSW by postcode or council (NSW Department of Communities and Justice), QLD by suburb or council (Residential Tenancies Authority), WA by locality (calculated by DwellDelta from the Government of Western Australia's bond records). Each CC BY 4.0. area or council names the place the question is about; with neither, the answer is the state's own figure. The figures are new-bond medians, not advertised rents. Each state measures in its own way, so the states are not one series: their figures cannot be added together or compared as one. Each answer states its quarter, its source line and the source's limits. Victoria is in vic_rents. For NSW and QLD, dwelling_type or bedrooms (or both) give the publisher's figure for that kind of home instead - a two-bedroom unit, a three-bedroom house. Only combinations the publisher reports are answered: one with no published median is said to have none, and neither another area's figure nor the all-dwellings figure stands in for it. Many such figures rest on few bonds. WA has no figures by dwelling type or bedrooms.

state.description: NSW, QLD or WA - one state per call

area.description: NSW: a four-digit postcode (a suburb name returns its postcodes to try). QLD: a suburb. WA: a locality. Part of a suburb or locality name works

council.description: A council (NSW or QLD), or part of its name

dwelling_type.description: NSW and QLD only. NSW (DCJ's labels): House, Townhouse, Flat/Unit, Other. QLD (the RTA's): Flat, House, Townhouse. 'unit' and 'apartment' are read as flat/unit. Without bedrooms, every size the publisher reports for that type is given

bedrooms.description: NSW and QLD only: a number of bedrooms, as '2' or '2 bedrooms'. NSW also has Bedsitter, and 4 means DCJ's '4 or more Bedrooms'; a number above 4 is answered under that label too, and the answer says it is not for that number alone. QLD: the RTA publishes flats of 1 to 3, houses of 2 to 4 and town houses of 2 to 3, and does not define its labels - reading the number as bedrooms is DwellDelta's. A plus means 'or more', which only DCJ's 4 has: '3+', and any 'N+' for QLD, is refused, not answered as exactly N. Without dwelling_type, every type the publisher reports at that size is given

annotations.title: NSW, Queensland and WA rents by postcode, suburb or locality

tools.name: nsw_sale_prices
tools.description: Median sale price of the dwellings sold in the latest reported quarter in NSW, with the quartiles, the number of sales and the change on a year before, by postcode or council and by dwelling type - all dwellings, non_strata (separate houses) and strata (units, town houses, villas). From the NSW Department of Communities and Justice's Rent and Sales Report (CC BY 4.0). area or council names the place the question is about; with neither, the answer is the state's own figures. These are medians of homes sold: not asking prices, not valuations, and never what any one home sold for or is worth. A line marked UNUSUAL was set by a few very large sales or by many sales at one identical price, and is not a going price. A total noted as mostly a marked row's sales may be moved by them, and the file shows nothing more about it. A line with any other mark or note is not a going price either, and the file does not say why. Each answer names the dwelling type, the quarter and the source line, and states the limits.

area.description: A four-digit NSW postcode (a suburb name returns its postcodes to try)

council.description: An NSW council, or part of its name

dwelling_type.description: total, non_strata (houses) or strata (units, town houses, villas); without it, all three are given

annotations.title: NSW median sale prices by postcode or council

tools.name: contribute_rent
tools.description: Adds the user's own weekly rent, anonymously, to DwellDelta's NSW suburb rents - suburb, home type, bedrooms, rent and lease month; never an address, name or email. It takes two calls. The first stores and sends nothing: it returns consent text for the user to read, and a one-use token. The rent is sent only by a second call with the same details, that token and user_agreed: true, which is for when the user has said yes to that text. The tool is for a rent the user has asked to add, or has agreed to add on seeing the consent text - one rent, for one consent, never a batch of rents; never added on the user's behalf by default; and never a figure found online.

suburb.description: NSW suburb of the rented home, with its postcode, as "Newtown (2042)"

current_rent.description: Current weekly rent in Australian dollars

proposed_rent.description: Proposed new weekly rent, if there is one

whose.description: my_own_tenancy (the user rents it) or my_own_property (the user owns it). There is no value for a figure found online, which cannot be added.

consent_token.description: From the first call; without it, the call returns the consent text

user_agreed.description: true only if the user said yes to the consent text

annotations.title: Add the user's own rent (NSW), with their consent
